title: Golden Ratio φ and Conjugate ψ
content: The golden ratio φ = (1+√5)/2 ≈ 1.618 and its conjugate ψ = (1-√5)/2 ≈ -0.618 are the two roots of the characteristic equation x² - x - 1 = 0 of the Fibonacci recurrence. Together they satisfy Vieta's formulas: φ + ψ = 1 (sum of roots) and φ·ψ = -1 (product of roots). Both are declared noncomputable since they live in ℝ and involve √5.
mathContext: $\varphi = \frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2} \approx 1.618$, $\psi = \frac{1-\sqrt{5}}{2} \approx -0.618$. Both satisfy $x^2 = x + 1$, i.e., they are roots of $x^2 - x - 1 = 0$.

title: Algebraic Properties: φ² = φ+1 and Vieta's Formulas
content: The key algebraic facts are proved by ring_nf combined with Real.sq_sqrt. The defining property φ² = φ + 1 (and identically ψ² = ψ + 1) is what makes paired induction work in Binet's formula: the recurrence step reduces φ^(n+2) = φ^n · φ² = φ^n · (φ+1) = φ^(n+1) + φ^n, mirroring the Fibonacci recurrence. Vieta's formulas (φ+ψ=1, φψ=-1) reflect that φ and ψ are roots of x²-x-1=0.
mathContext: $\varphi^2 = \varphi + 1$, $\psi^2 = \psi + 1$, $\varphi + \psi = 1$, $\varphi\psi = -1$, $\varphi - \psi = \sqrt{5}$. The last identity is the key for the initial case of Binet's formula: $F_1 = (\varphi - \psi)/\sqrt{5} = \sqrt{5}/\sqrt{5} = 1$.

title: Binet's Formula: fib(n) = (φⁿ - ψⁿ)/√5
content: Binet's formula is proved by paired induction: simultaneously prove the formula for fib(n) and fib(n+1). The base case uses fib(0)=0=(1-1)/√5 and fib(1)=1=(φ-ψ)/√5=√5/√5. The inductive step uses the Fibonacci recurrence fib(n+2)=fib(n)+fib(n+1) and the algebraic identities φ²=φ+1, ψ²=ψ+1. The formula simultaneously encodes the exact integer value (discrete) and continuous exponential growth governed by φ.
mathContext: $F_n = \frac{\varphi^n - \psi^n}{\sqrt{5}}$ for all $n \geq 0$. Proof by paired induction: assume $F_n = \frac{\varphi^n - \psi^n}{\sqrt{5}}$ and $F_{n+1} = \frac{\varphi^{n+1} - \psi^{n+1}}{\sqrt{5}}$; then $F_{n+2} = F_n + F_{n+1} = \frac{(\varphi^n + \varphi^{n+1}) - (\psi^n + \psi^{n+1})}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{\varphi^n(1+\varphi) - \psi^n(1+\psi)}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{\varphi^{n+2} - \psi^{n+2}}{\sqrt{5}}$.

title: Five-Step Fibonacci Identity: fib(5k+7) ≥ 10·fib(5k+2)
content: The arithmetic core of Part I. fib_add_five establishes fib(n+5) = 5·fib(n+1) + 3·fib(n) by unfolding four applications of the recurrence and letting omega close by linear arithmetic. fib_five_step_growth then shows fib(5k+7) ≥ 10·fib(5k+2) by expanding all intermediate Fibonacci values and using monotonicity fib(5k) ≤ fib(5k+1). The key inequality fib(5k+7) = 8·fib(5k+2) + 5·fib(5k+1) ≥ 10·fib(5k+2) uses 3·fib(5k+1) ≥ 2·fib(5k).

title: fib(5k+2) ≥ 10^k and the Unrestricted Lamé Bound
content: fib_ge_pow10_general proves 10^k ≤ fib(5k+2) for all k by induction, using the multiplicative growth lemma as the inductive step: 10^(k+1) = 10·10^k ≤ 10·fib(5k+2) ≤ fib(5k+7) = fib(5(k+1)+2). The Lamé bound then follows: given b > 0 with d = ⌊log₁₀ b⌋, we have b < 10^(d+1) ≤ fib(5(d+1)+2), and the parent module's lame_step_bound converts this Fibonacci lower bound into a step count upper bound.
mathContext: $F_{5k+2} \geq 10^k$ for all $k \geq 0$. Combined with $b < 10^{d+1}$ where $d = \lfloor \log_{10} b \rfloor$: $b < F_{5(d+1)+2}$, so the Euclidean algorithm on $b$ takes at most $5(d+1)-1 \leq 5 \cdot \text{decimalDigits}(b)$ steps.

title: φ⁵ > 10: The Golden Ratio Explanation for 5 Digits
content: The computation φ⁵ = 5φ+3 > 10 is the geometric reason Lamé's bound has coefficient 5: each 5-step block in the Fibonacci sequence multiplies by φ⁵ > 10, consuming exactly one decimal digit. The proof reduces powers of φ using φ² = φ+1 iteratively (phi_pow3, phi_pow4, phi_pow5), then bounds φ > 7/5 from √5 > 9/5 (itself from √5·√5 = 5 and √5 > 0). The numerical value φ⁵ ≈ 11.09 explains why the bound is not tight at 4 digits.

title: Nearest Integer Property: fib(n) = round(φⁿ/√5)
content: Since |ψ| < 1, we have |ψ^n| ≤ 1 for all n ≥ 0, and the Binet formula gives |fib(n) - φⁿ/√5| = |ψⁿ|/√5 ≤ 1/√5 < 1/2 (since √5 > 2). This means fib(n) is exactly the nearest integer to φⁿ/√5, giving a closed-form approximation accurate to within 1/2. The proof uses abs_psi_lt_one (|ψ| < 1 from √5 < 3 and √5 > 1), then combines pow_le_one with bounds on √5.
mathContext: $|F_n - \varphi^n/\sqrt{5}| = |\psi|^n/\sqrt{5} \leq 1/\sqrt{5} < 1/2$, so $F_n = \text{round}(\varphi^n/\sqrt{5})$. This gives the Fibonacci numbers as round($\varphi^n / 2.236\ldots$) for all $n$.
